# M4 metrics: events and plays (synthetic)

**Synthetic data only.** Re-measured 2026-10-06 on hfbox. Numbers: `metrics.json` (generated by
`eval/split.py`). The scripts that produced them are in `eval/`. M1 and M5 use the same runs.

## Code state

The laptop working tree at HEAD `5b5bd2b`, plus uncommitted work in progress. These courtcam
files differ from HEAD: `detect.py`, `pose.py`, `triggers.py`, `pyproject.toml`, `README.md` and
`tests/test_pipeline.py`, plus the new `extras.py`. The source changes only add import guards
for the optional extras, so none of them changes detection, pose, events, triggers or plays.

## Data

Nine 90 s clips, generated during this run by `courtcam synth --duration 90` (1280x720, 30 fps):

- basketball half court, seeds 7 and 11
- basketball full court, seed 7
- badminton doubles, seeds 7 and 11
- pickleball doubles, seeds 7 and 11
- volleyball indoor, seeds 7 and 11

The voice lines come from `samples/synthetic/voice`.

## Commands

Run these on the box, from a copy of the tree:

```bash
mkdir -p _m && cp docs/evidence/M4/eval/* _m/
bash _m/run_metrics.sh gen    # courtcam synth, 9 clips
bash _m/run_metrics.sh gt     # synthetic detector + GT poses (run1.py), whisper-small triggers (run_trig.py), eval_synth.py
bash _m/run_metrics.sh yolo   # YOLO detect (yolo11m) + YOLO pose (yolo11m-pose), same triggers and eval
bash _m/run_metrics.sh vit    # rerun.py: pose -> plays again on the YOLO tracks with ViTPose (vitpose-base-simple)
bash _m/run_metrics.sh mot    # courtcam eval (CLEAR-MOT / IDF1) on the five seed-7 scenes, for M1
python _m/agg.py _m/out > _m/agg.json && python _m/split.py _m/agg.json <dest> _m/meta.json
```

`eval_synth.py` (taken from the accuracy pass) matches events to the synthetic truth with
these windows:

- **Shots:** ±1.5 s to the ball at the rim.
- **Possession changes:** ±2.5 s, same team.
- **Points:** ±1.5 s.
- **Contacts:** ±0.15 s.
- **Rallies and plays:** temporal IoU ≥ 0.5. Plays use the sport's primary grammar.

### What the M4 regression was

- **GT-pose shots 23 → 18 of 27:** the accuracy pass (35e7909) lowered the release arm
  line to 0.2 torso below the shoulders (`shot.release_up_min: -0.2`). That lengthens
  every measured release: a synthetic jump shot is 0.83-0.87 s above the nose but
  0.90-0.93 s above the new line, past `release_max_s: 0.9`, so 5 releases were thrown
  out as "held". Bisected: old events code (60f140e) on today's clips gives 23; HEAD
  gives 18; HEAD with `release_up_min: null` gives 23; switching off the camera hoop
  (17) or the MAD floor (18, 4 false) does not bring them back. The clips are not the
  cause (the M4-era clips give the same counts with either code). Fix:
  `shot.release_max_s: 1.0` in basketball.yaml (1.0, 1.1, 1.2 and 1.5 all give 23 GT and
  21 YOLO). Real Kennesaw 240 s (local) stays at 3 shots, all real.
- **YOLO rallies P 0.97 / R 0.88 at M4:** not a regression in code since M4. The M4
  YOLO run kept on the box (05:42 UTC, before the M4 commit 4c6c02a at 06:36 UTC) was
  made with `rally.audio_fusion` on; the M4 commit shipped it off for badminton and
  pickleball (D-51: real shuttle hits gave P/R 0.36 fused). Re-running
  today's events stage on that run's stored outputs gives P 0.75 / R 0.69 with both the
  M4 commit's code and HEAD, and P 0.88 / R 0.81 (exactly the stored run) with fusion
  on. GT-pose rallies were P 0.73 / R 0.67 at M4 too.
- **Fix for rallies without fusion:** players stop running before the last shot lands,
  so a motion rally ended ~1.2 s early. A strong onset within `onset_pad_s` after the
  motion end now extends the rally past it (`rally.audio_extend_end`, never shrinks or
  splits a rally). Real badminton 240 s (14 hand-labelled rallies, local footage):
  12/14 at P 1.00 before and after; full fusion there is 5/14. The cost: onsets after
  the last hit (the landing) now count as contacts, so contact precision drops (table).

### Pickleball side-out scoring (doubles)

`rally.side_out: true` in pickleball.yaml: `events.assign_winners` follows USA Pickleball
Official Rulebook (2025) 4.B.6 (the game's starting server serves alone, as "Second
Server"; after a side out the First Server, then the Second Server) and Section 1 (only
the serving side scores). The same side serving next with the partner serving means the
first server lost the rally; a point's `points` is 0 when the receivers won, and
`plays.score_timeline` adds `points`. The synthetic generator uses rally scoring (the
rally winner always serves next, rotating servers), so on synthetic pickleball the
side-out rule misreads a winning team's server rotation as a lost rally. The rule
itself is checked by `tests/test_plays.py::test_side_out_doubles_second_server`.

- GT poses, pickleball_doubles_s7, pickleball_doubles_s11: winner_ok / winner_known 9/13 as shipped vs 12/13 with `pickleball rally.side_out=false`
- YOLO detect + pose, pickleball_doubles_s7, pickleball_doubles_s11: winner_ok / winner_known 8/13 as shipped vs 10/13 with `pickleball rally.side_out=false`

### Contact sides (open item: `side_ok` near chance)

`rally.one_touch: true` (badminton, pickleball): contact sides alternate through a
rally, anchored on the side most per-contact wrist-speed guesses agree with; the hitter
is then the fastest wrists on that side. Volleyball (up to 3 touches a side) keeps the
per-contact guess. Not measured on real footage (no contact labels); a real bounce
loud enough to pass `contact_min_strength` would shift the parity for the rest of the
rally.

- GT poses, badminton_doubles_s7, badminton_doubles_s11, pickleball_doubles_s7, pickleball_doubles_s11: side_ok / tp 158/177 as shipped vs 106/177 with `rally.one_touch=false`
- YOLO detect + pose, badminton_doubles_s7, badminton_doubles_s11, pickleball_doubles_s7, pickleball_doubles_s11: side_ok / tp 112/177 as shipped vs 92/177 with `rally.one_touch=false`
- GT poses, badminton_doubles_s7, badminton_doubles_s11, pickleball_doubles_s7, pickleball_doubles_s11: hitter_ok / tp 133/177 as shipped vs 94/177 with `rally.one_touch=false`
- YOLO detect + pose, badminton_doubles_s7, badminton_doubles_s11, pickleball_doubles_s7, pickleball_doubles_s11: hitter_ok / tp 71/177 as shipped vs 65/177 with `rally.one_touch=false`

Not attempted: volleyball attack (P 0.30 GT / 0.10 YOLO, unchanged).

Reading: no tracking or events row moved by more than 0.02 in the wrong direction except the
basketball shot attribution rows, which a bisect traced to identity v2. The same four
basketball YOLO/GT clips rerun with 9b777bb's courtcam but 005cf87's `identity.py` give
exactly the events-v2 numbers, so the differences are all identity v2. With the GT detector,
the jersey cut splits perfect tracks (basketball half s11: tracks 5, 6, 9 and 10 are cut and
relinked; one piece of 10 (team 0) ends up in the same player as a piece of 9 (team 1)),
which renumbers players and puts one shooter on the wrong tracklet (2 vs 3 points 23 → 22). Net gains from identity v2 under
YOLO: possession change 22 → 23 TP, cause right 13/22 → 15/23, plays P 0.90 → 0.92, attack
1 → 2 TP. Volleyball, badminton and pickleball rows are unchanged by identity v2.
